translation_notes: prefixes: OWL->owl, RDFS->rdfs, RDF->rdf, SKOS->skos (OWL stays unused before and after, same as in original.py -- it comes from the file's own import line, not from anything this region reads).

Despite the name, `select_first_value` does NOT read-then-reuse a first value anywhere (no `g.value`, `next(...)`, `.first()`-shaped call): both rdf_ops this stratum cares about are genuinely boolean existence tests -- `not any(seed_graph.objects(s_can, p_can))` and `(s_can, p_can, o_can) not in seed_graph` -- so `bool(m{ })` is not a downgrade here, it is what the code actually does. The 'first value wins' behaviour is an emergent property of running the SAME existence guard once per source triple inside the surrounding for-loop (whichever source triple for a given (subject, predicate) is processed first satisfies the guard and gets adopted, blocking the rest) -- not a single call this study could credit to `.first()`/`.one()`/`next()`. Checked per the batch's LARGEUR DU CRITERE instruction; the fear was unfounded on this region.

Two DIFFERENT existence idioms in one region, both -> bool(m{ }): fusable branch `not any(seed_graph.objects(s_can, p_can))` -> `not bool(m{ {s_can} {p_can} ?o })` (rdflib's predicate+object-position `.objects(s, p)` becomes a 2-bound-term/1-variable pattern); non-fusable branch `(s_can, p_can, o_can) not in seed_graph` -> `not bool(m{ {s_can} {p_can} {o_can} })` (all three terms bound, the textbook `(s, p, o) in g` idiom). Both `.add()` calls -> `+{ {s_can} {p_can} {o_can} }` under a single `@graph seed_graph` declared once, right after `seed_graph` is built and never reassigned after (so the @graph-captures-a-value caveat in SS2bis does not bite).

NOT translated, deliberately: `source_graph.parse(...)`/`seed_graph.parse(...)`/`seed_graph.serialize(...)` (serialize_parse: file I/O, no island form); `seed_graph.subjects(unique=True)` (graph_read: reads ALL subjects with a uniqueness flag, not covered by any idiom in INSTRUCTIONS.md SS2's table -- `m{ ?s ?p ?o }` would change both the read's shape and its dedup semantics, so it stays a plain rdflib call); `for s, p, o in source_graph:` (plain whole-graph iteration, not a bound-pattern match, and not one of the named strata idioms either -- left as Python). `Graph()` constructor calls are never an island form (g{ } is for INLINE Turtle literals, not `Graph()`).

Restored a missing binding, not just a missing import: `TrackRecord` is used (`TrackRecord(subject=...)`, `List[TrackRecord]`) but never imported anywhere in the extracted window -- it is defined in the SAME source file at preference.py:20-25, just above the extraction boundary (confirmed via `gh api` at the pinned commit), so this is the 163-region 'liaison manquante' case (SS6), restored via context_shim.py rather than treated as a reason to exclude.

context_shim.py: `kgpipe`/`kgpipe_tasks` (first-party) and `kgcore` (an external dependency of this region's file) are BOTH absent from PyPI (`pip index versions kgpipe` / `kgcore` -> 'No matching distribution found' for each) -- classification (a) is not available for either, this is genuinely (b): not installable, so the whole call chain is shimmed rather than partially excluded. `TrackRecord` is reproduced as a plain dataclass (not pydantic, which is also not installed) with a `__post_init__` coercing every field to `str`, reproducing pydantic's own coercion of the `URIRef`/`Literal` values (both `str` subclasses in rdflib) the region actually passes into fields the real class declares as `str` -- needed so `model_dump()` stays JSON-serialisable for the `json.dump(..., default=...)` calls further down, which are otherwise untouched. `Registry.task` is simplified to the identity decorator: the real one (kgpipe/common/registry.py:67-82) wraps the function into a `KgTask` and registers it globally, machinery this region's RDF operations do not depend on. `OntologyUtil.load_ontology_from_file` reads a small JSON file the driver writes instead of a real ontology file, giving `ontology.properties[i].uri`/`.max_cardinality` the same shape preference.py:33-34 reads. `TARGET_ONTOLOGY_NAMESPACE` is copied verbatim from kgpipe/common/config.py:18 (`"http://kg.org/ontology/"`).

demo() harness (identical both sides): writes source/target N-Triples to a fresh temp dir, points OntologyUtil at a JSON ontology, runs the region, returns the graph re-parsed from outputs['output'].path -- since `select_first_value` only communicates through files, not return values or in-memory graphs. Fixture subjects s1/s2 give both directions of the fusable-branch check (already-has-a-value -> block; absent -> add); s3 gives the one discriminating direction of the non-fusable-branch check plus proves the OBJECT is part of its pattern (a same-subject/-predicate neighbour with a DIFFERENT object must still be added); s4 is an exact-duplicate case included for realism though it cannot discriminate (see next note); s5 has a predicate outside allowed_predicates and must be skipped entirely, guarding against an accidentally-widened pattern; s6 (added after the sabotage below) proves the fusable check's PREDICATE is part of its pattern, not just the subject.

A genuine, region-specific finding, not a driver limitation: the non-fusable branch's guard `(s, p, o) not in seed_graph` only ever gates a `.add()` of that SAME (s, p, o), and `Graph.add` is idempotent (a set) -- so when the triple is ALREADY present, the guarded and unguarded outcomes are IDENTICAL regardless of what the guard decides, and no fixture built from this region's own observable output (the final graph, or the untouched selected/discarded lists, which this branch never appends to) can discriminate a correct translation from one that flipped that one direction. Only the 'wrongly treats an absent triple as present' direction is observable (a missing triple in the result), and case s3 exercises exactly that. Confirmed empirically below.

Deliberately broke the translation twice to confirm rdfeval check catches what it can: (1) fusable-branch pattern `{s_can} {p_can} ?o` -> `{s_can} ?anyp ?o` (dropped the predicate): FIRST attempt with only s1/s2/s3/s4/s5 in the fixture stayed GREEN -- s1's only seed triple already IS the label triple and s2 has no seed triple at all, so 'any predicate' and 'this predicate' coincide by accident for both; only after adding s6 (seed has s6 under an UNRELATED predicate) did it go FAIL call[0].result: graphs not isomorphic (7 vs 6 triples) -- s6's rdfs:label was wrongly withheld. This is itself a finding: a fixture can look adequate (multiple subjects, both branches) while still missing the one case that separates a correct pattern from an over-generalised one. (2) non-fusable-branch pattern `{s_can} {p_can} {o_can}` -> `{s_can} {p_can} ?anyo` (dropped the object): FAIL call[0].result: graphs not isomorphic (7 vs 6 triples) -- s3's second altLabel value was wrongly withheld, confirming the object-specificity claim above. Both restored, check is green again.
